examples: See every computer in the pack and every ssh host in one list, with the ones that need a look pulled into a red group.
Open a computer you reach over ssh and read its ssh facts, copy the ssh command and say which computer an ssh host belongs to.
Find the computer with the most free cpu before you start a big job.
how_to: Open pack, computers: the rail filters the list, the find field searches name, ssh login and tools, and sort and the cards or list switch sit in the bar.
Click a computer to open its reading pane: overview, projects, link and ssh tabs; escape closes the pane and the arrow keys move between computers.
On the ssh tab, pick the computer an ssh host belongs to; the pack keeps your pick instead of guessing from the name.
Press the wolf button on a computer, then confirm, to make it the pack leader.
Press add a computer: one entry with four routes (a code, over ssh, an ssh host only, pair an older computer).
The pack settings panel on the right folds into the gear in the title strip; it holds the pack name, advertising, membership or join a pack, show a code and rotate key.
media_exempt: The roster needs a live pack of two or more computers and an ssh host to show cards, the red needs a look group and the ssh tab; the capture is recorded with the release run.
name: Pack roster
summary: the pack page's computers and ssh tabs are one roster of computer cards with a reading pane per computer and a pack settings panel that folds into a gear.
where: Pack, computers tab (#pack, with #pack/ssh landing on the over ssh filter).
